chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

When you are in the state of Ihram in the open land (al-Hill) and you kill game between yourself and the distance of al-Bareed to the Sanctuary (al-Haram), then upon you is its compensation. If you blind its eye or break its horn, you give charity.

key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land (as opposed to the sacred precincts of the Haram)
key_terms.مُحِلًّا: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing game while in Ihram in the open land before reaching the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the liability of Jaza' (compensation) for game killed in the open land (al-Hill) during Ihram, distinguishing it from the stricter rules within the Sanctuary boundaries. It highlights the juristic principle that specific injuries, such as blinding the eye or breaking the horn, trigger a mandatory charity (Sadaqah) as a form of expiation, reflecting the detailed fiqh of the Imams regarding ritual purity and hunting regulations.
